label: copy-phase input c (fed-back output c), from the 2nd copied token on
explanation: Fires only when the input token is c during the copy phase, i.e. the model just output c and it is fed back. Every activation has in_tok == c in the copy phase; it never fires on any other token, in the original phase, or at the delimiter. It is weak or absent when the fed-back c is the first original token (recall_idx 1, where only about 0.6% of steps fire), and fires reliably from recall_idx 2 onward. The strongest activations occur in sequences with an adjacent c c pair, on the first copied c of that pair, with the following c weaker. Low-activation cases are mostly c inputs early in the copy phase.

issues: One number in the explanation is wrong. It says 'only about 0.6% of those steps fire' for fed-back c at recall_idx 1, but the predicate (phase==2)&(in_tok==c)&(recall_idx==1) has precision 0.171 on dev (2835 of 16540 steps fire, about 17%). The 0.6% is the firing rate over ALL recall_idx-1 steps, not over the c steps. The qualitative point still holds: those activations are weak, with mass recall 0.013 and 13% of the bottom activation quartile, so leaving them out of the predicate is reasonable.

Every exclusivity claim checks out on dev. Phase 'original' and the delimiter step have 0 activations. in_tok is c for 100% of active steps. 'Copy phase and input c' gives precision 0.783, recall 1.0, F1 0.878, matching the reported figures.

The 'c c' claim checks out. Restricting to out_tok==c (the first copied c of an adjacent pair) gives precision 1.0 and carries 7.5% of the mass on only 3.4% of the active steps. The top examples show the second c of the pair weaker.

On test, the predicate scores precision 0.920, recall 0.958, F1 0.939 and mass recall 0.986, matching the report. Missed activations on test (2972, 1.4% of the mass) are almost all c fed back as the first original token (recall_idx 1). They are weak and consistent with the explanation.

The false positives (5963 on test) are mostly graded, not a separate class. Precision varies with the token being output next: about 0.68-0.80 when out_tok is p, s, m, b or i, and about 0.98-0.99 when it is a, e, j, q, t, u, v, w or y. Excluding the low-precision tokens lowers test F1 (0.912 or 0.857, against 0.939). So this modulation does not support a better predicate; it is a minor magnitude effect the label does not mention.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
